Detecting multiband microwave (MW) and terahertz (THz) photoelectric properties is vital for advancing quantum technology and quantum chemistry. While high-frequency THz measurements are typically managed using electro-optic sampling, this approach struggles with limited sensitivity and bandwidth, rendering it inadequate for THz fields. Conversely, RF heterodyne techniques dominate standard sensitivity levels but fail to operate at THz frequencies due to hardware limitations in generating local-oscillator signals. We introduce an innovative Rydberg atom sensing framework capable of simultaneously measuring field strength in the MW and THz regimes with high resolution and precision. This method eliminates the need for traditional heterodyne instrumentation by utilizing a Rydberg atom as a selective, tunable absorber of electromagnetic radiation. Furthermore, it employs a locked microwave oscillator to define a continuous resonance curve across the target frequency spectrum; when exposed to external radiation, this curve undergoes frequency and strength shifts proportional to the signals detected. By leveraging the extreme polarizability of Rydberg atoms at these frequencies, the system achieves not only the co-detection of THz and RF components but also accurately determines their phase relationships.

The low surface brightness (LSB) spiral UGC 8839 exhibits extreme off-axis star formation, a characteristic common among such galaxies. Although the origin of this phenomenon remains debated, we propose that it is driven by global tidal forces. Analysis of HI data reveals a global warp in UGC 8839's disk, a feature corroborated by a significant, asymmetric halo of neutral hydrogen. This halo is most pronounced on the north-east side, where a massive, irregular star-forming complex exists. We suggest a feedback loop wherein the warp concentrates gas and triggers star formation, with resulting stellar feedback further perturbing the disk and enhancing the warp. This mechanism likely extends to other warp-associated star-forming halos found in LSB galaxies.

The result demonstrates that the Hausdorff dimension of the set of rapidly escaping points for a quasiregular mapping on ${\mathbb R}^3$ can be any value in the range $[1,3]$. Moreover, under specific growth conditions, the dimension of the associated Julia set for these maps is also determined.

The MAVEN/NGIMS instrument detects gravity waves (GWs) within Mars' upper atmosphere through molecular density fluctuations. As GW amplitude directly influences MARSIS's MNGIMS signal strength, understanding these factors is vital for developing robust modeling and inversion techniques. This study examines GW characteristics across latitudes and local times using the MARSIS/NGIMS dataset alongside meteorological global hemispheric models (GHMMs) that estimate atmospheric stability and vertical wind shear. Results reveal a correlation between signal intensity and atmospheric stability, peaking near the equator and polar regions while dipping in mid-latitudes. Additionally, an analysis of signal intensity against vertical wind shear and atmospheric stability shows that density variations are more strongly linked to stability than to wind shear.

The LHC has been operating since 2010, with its first three years dedicated to beam commissioning and tests, meaning Ultra-Peripheral Collisions (UPCs) of $pp$ and $PbPb$ first became available in the LHCb experiment during Run I. A photon-photon induced J/$\psi$$\overline{}$X signal was detected in the single $p$-$p$ mode during this initial phase. This overview will focus on the photon-photon J/$\psi$$\

We introduce a model for generating short-phase audio characterized by its ability to capture statistical distributions of phonemes, acoustic tones, and musical notes. Achieved through sampling discrete variables via a variational autoencoder (VAE) in a wholly discrete latent space, our approach eliminates the need for discrete latent variable methods like GMM-VAEs while effectively preventing acoustically inconsistent artifacts often seen in fully generative approaches. The resulting output consists of realistic combinations of different acoustic tones, musical pitches, and spoken sounds. The model's capacity to represent and sample these discrete elements is supported by evaluations using perceptual quality metrics and analyses of acoustic feature embeddings. Furthermore, our method demonstrates strong generalization across a variety of acoustic domains, including models trained specifically on musical instruments or individual voice identities to generate varied tones, pitches, and phonemes.

The recent resurgence of Recurrent Networks for sequential tasks, such as language modeling and machine translation, is largely attributed to the gated network architectures they employ. We propose a new architecture for handling sequences that does not rely on gating mechanisms; instead, it achieves significant performance gains across application domains previously, and exceeds the results achieved by existing models including the LSTM.

This study introduces the concept of "economic irreversibility" asIrreversible, where delayed implementing effective containment strategies leads to permanent, cumulative harm to the economy that cannot be undone. Specifically, the time spent before enacting policies capable of bringing the effective reproduction number ($R_t$) below one generates lasting damage. The authors model this phenomenon using a real options framework applied to an $R$-below-one state, illustrating how risk-averse behavior inherently creates a delay in optimal reaction times. By examining the relationship between the rate of irreversible damage and the parameters of the epidemic model, the work demonstrates that, unlike in standard options where a higher cost of time always accelerates action, the necessary conditions for timely pandemic response are not straightforward. The study concludes by outlining the specific characteristics of the optimal policy trajectory and discussing how such policy responds to variations in the cost of delays, the potential scale of the outbreak, and the fluctuating current level of infections.

We introduce a practical, data-localized algorithm designed to calculate Shapley values for training data in machine learning models. This approach represents data Shapley scores as solutions to linear systems of equations and resolves them using the conjugate gradient method, requiring only polynomial time. Our methodology is fully distributed, allowing for the processing of massive datasets without transferring data outside their original environments, thereby ensuring privacy and security. We have implemented this sheraloy package in Python and evaluated its performance against synthetic and real-world benchmarks. Our computational experiments demonstrate that the system efficiently handles large-scale scenarios involving over 10 million data points.

We establish the relationships within multiple seemingly independent mathematical domains, including enumerative algebraic geometry, combinatorics, algebraic statistics, and topology. This study centers on discrete invariants that closely resemble Ltorentzn polynomials, with the primary conceptual link across these disciplines being a space defined by linear matrices.

This research investigates the anomalous Hall effect in three triangular antiferromagnetic materials—Mn$_3$Sn, Mn$_3$Ge, and Cu$_3$MnS$_2$—utilizing both experimental measurements and theoretical modeling. Experimentally, we observe that applying pressure significantly amplifies the anomalous Hall effect in all three samples: a hydrostatic pressure of 2 GPa produces effects comparable to those of 30 nm-thin epitaxial layers in Mn$_3$Sn and Mn$_3$Ge, while a 2D layer-strain in Cu$_3$MnS$_2$ yields similar outcomes to that pressure. To analyze these findings, we employed spin-orbit coupling Hamiltonians with spin-wave approximations to model the magnetic ground states and transport properties. Our calculations reveal that the observed enhancement stems from the interplay between the spin-orbit coupling and pressure or strain-induced alterations in bond lengths and angles. Furthermore, the results illustrate that the specific arrangements of these three distinct antiferromagnetic systems occupy diverse positions within the parameter space, with Mn$_3$Sn and the strained variants in Cu$_3$MnS$_2$ exhibiting steepest slopes that promise significant gains in future optimizations. Ultimately, this study offers a strategic framework for manipulating magnetotransport characteristics in other magnetically ordered systems through the application of mechanical stress.

Extracting relations between entities within text is a pivotal task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) with broad-ranging applications. While recent years have seen significant strides in RE due to the surge in deep learning methods, these models depend heavily on vast amounts of labeled data, creating a bottleneck for domains where such labels are sparse or nonexistent. To address this, this paper explores the potential of incorporating external knowledge bases—specifically Wikidata—to augment training. Wikidata offers both an extensive encyclopedia of entity information and a comprehensive set of entity relationship definitions. Wikidata is enriched with entity mentions from the target dataset to facilitate integration. Three distinct fusion strategies are examined to combine this auxiliary information effectively. Tests across eight datasets highlight scenarios involving both seen and unseen ReLO settings. Results indicate that leveraging Wikidata enhances modeling performance, with proposed fusion methods outperforming baseline approaches across seven out of eight tested datasets. The methodology is open-source and accessible via the repository: https://github.com/lucy-zhang-wiki/RE-with-Wikidata.

This study examines a Steklov-Robin eigenvalue problem involving Laplacian in the context of annular domains within $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($ n\ge 2$) and considers the scenario where the Steklov parameter $\lambda_{\mathfrak{S}}$ and the Robin parameter $\sigma$ are non-constant functions. The primary objective is to establish a combinatorial formula for counting the first eigenvalue, denoted as $ \lambda_{1}$, under specific constraints on $\sigma$ and $\lambda_{\mathfrak{S}}$. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that $ \lambda_{1}$ is simple, positive, and maintains its positivity.

Graph theory addresses a wide range of challenges, and its algorithms have been adapted to graph-like structures such as hypergraphs. Currently, there is no dedicated library of proven algorithms for these. The goal of the Hyper-Project is to resolve this library deficit, and the authors are releasing the Hyper: A Python implementation of algorithms for general graph-based objects. The paper provides a detailed overview of the package's features and offers a comprehensive suite of examples.

Intelligent systems are increasingly capable of analyzing medical imaging data to detect diseases, diagnose conditions, and plan treatments. While these models often perform well given the abundance of training images, they typically fail to generalize effectively to new data. This limitation often stems from the fact that most algorithms treat images as unordered collections of pixels, ignoring the underlying anatomical structures. This work introduces a new framework for medical image analysis that explicitly integrates anatomical structures into the model. By representing images as graphs where tissue types define the edges, this approach naturally captures anatomical information. Furthermore, we developed and applied a new, approximately linear-time algorithm for maximum flow computation on anatomy-specific graphs. Experiments across multiple datasets, including those for cardiac and brain analysis, demonstrate that this framework can effectively represent anatomical knowledge and outperform standard performance on these medical tasks.

We demonstrate that any taut foliation on an irreducible, orientable closed 3-manifold $M$ possesses an Euler class magnitude that meets the lower bound of one-seventh of the Thurston norm of the two-skeleton of the foliation. Additionally, we examine taut foliations on prime 3-manifolds which achieve this bound exactly. Our findings establish that a tight contact structure on such an irreducible, orientable closed 3-manifold $M$ is T2 (as defined by Lutz and Martinet) if and only if the Euler class magnitude strictly surpasses one-third of the minimum Euler number found within the two-spines of the contact structure.

This work introduces a robust metric for characterizing unidirectional emission in microcavity lasers. While Shannon entropy applied to far-field distributions—calculated within polar coordinates to ascertain directional symmetry and its stability against parameter-induced deformationsoffers superior performance compared to conventional methods—it is particularly effective for evaluating laser emission unidirectionality.

This paper offers a novel analysis of cryptocurrency performance by comparing them to major financial assets like equities, bonds, and commodities. Utilizing dynamic factor models, we evaluate both return predictability and the stability of risk premiums. Our findings indicate that while cryptocurrencies may achieve predictability similar to traditional assets, risk premiums exhibit significantly greater volatility. This suggests that, at this stage, cryptocurrencies are not yet fully integrated into standard financial markets. Furthermore, we uncover pronounced differences in risk premium stability among individual cryptocurrencies, implying that only a select few have the market presence necessary for potential future acceptance. These insights carry important implications for asset allocation strategies and the broader adoption of digital currencies.

We investigate large deviations over finite time intervals for the one-dimensional directed polymer in the Kopczewsky (KPZ) universality class, focusing on cases where spatial length L diverges. Using the Tazaki–Toyota framework, we derive explicit expressions for the large deviation functional across all h. Our approach begins with an exact reformulation of the partition function as a determinant of a stochastic differential equation, which is subsequently solved explicitly. This method validates previous research conducted by Airault and Kappeler as well as by Popov.

Compressive turbulence within the solar wind has been observed across multiple spatial scales by both spacecraft missions and ground-based instruments. Although various theories attempt to explain the resulting morphological density spectra, no single model fully accounts for all data. We propose a unified framework grounded in compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), where density fluctuations arise from the coupling between compressive and incompressible flows. Within this scenario, fluctuations at inertial scales stem from the MHD wave background, while fluctuations at dissipation scales result from the transition of Alfvén waves to switchback structures. Merging these distinct regimes produces a density spectrum form $k^{-\beta}$ where the exponent $\beta = \frac{2}{3}\alpha + \frac{1}{3}$; notably, this aligns closely with solar wind measurements showing $k^{-1.6}$. Furthermore, this theoretical prediction of the compressible/inductive partitioning is testable through proposed multi-scale observations.

The unique pulse coherence of X-rays in the few- to tens-of-nanometer wavelength range is essential for numerous applications, ranging from high-resolution coherent diffraction imaging of biological samples to probing nonlinear quantum effects in matter via synchrotron light and early-stage femtosecond fission gases. Current facilities at the LCLS, EuFEL, and SACLA already provide hard X-rays with picosecond coherence times, a benchmark expected to improve significantly with upcoming investments in seed lasers and optical cavities that will shrink coherence durations to approximately 100 femtoseconds. This review examines the coherence characteristics of self-amplified spontaneous emission (FELs) by analyzing the dynamics of microbunches and small-scale fluctuations, with a specific focus on the roles of seed lasers, microbunch length, and energy jitters. We also explore strategies for generating ultra-short, coherent pulses by modulating the magnetic field to induce chirp and subsequent compression, a technique demonstrated to be highly effective using pre-seeded FELs. This approach promises a pathway to achieving coherence times well below 10 femtoseconds, a capability anticipated from all third-generation free-electron lasers by 2030.

This work examines boundary layer flow and convection within an isothermal cavity subjected to a vertical temperature difference, anchored on lower and upper horizontal plates while bounded laterally by adiabatic vertical walls. The governing equations for mass, momentum, and energy conservation are solved numerically using a finite difference method with second-order accuracy, employing the staggered grid approach. Both the primary and secondary numerical methods utilize the Thomas algorithm. Boundary conditions for velocity and thermal parameters are implemented using a third-order formulation. The study applies the Boussinesq approximation and adopts Darcy's model with zero permeation resistance to simulate buoyancy-driven currents. Results are presented across a range of Grashof numbers to characterize velocity and thermal profiles, as well as the associated heat transfer coefficients.

Gerrymandering represents the manipulation of electoral district boundaries within a representative government system to tilt election results in a party's favor. Although widely recognized as detrimental to democratic integrity, effectively detecting such manipulation remains challenging. This study introduces deep learning methodologies designed to identify gerrymandering by analyzing geographic maps represented as images. We investigate two distinct generative adversarial network (GAN) architectures: a super-resolution GAN that completes an image of districts by predicting boundary segments and an adversarial auto-encoder that processes encoded representations of current district maps. Experimental results utilizing these models in a controlled setting demonstrate successful gerrymandering detection and significantly surpass leading traditional techniques.

This study introduces a novel approach for identifying defects in images with repetitive patterns. The technique begins by generating the GHOG (Gradient-based HOG) feature for each image segment, followed by applying Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to establish baseline characteristics. An image is classified as defective if its feature vector significantly diverges from these baseline standards. HOG remains effective for patterned materials but suffers from precision issues in this context; consequently, the proposed PCA-integrated HOG method delivers superior accuracy for defect detection. Furthermore, we introduce new parameters to refine the PCA component, enabling robust detection across defects with varying intensities. Validation using the PCA-HHOG model on a database of fabric with flaws demonstrates competitive performance against existing methodologies.

Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has proven highly effective for autonomous driving tasks, yet the absence of an analytical framework to evaluate the efficiency of specific training strategies complicates optimization efforts. This study introduces a novelly formulated return function that enables the measurement of sample efficiency for deep reinforcement learning-based navigation. The function relies on an information-theoretic perspective, characterizing the return as the information accumulated by the policy relative to a return distribution. Notably, since this approach relies on analytical formulations, it facilitates evaluation at any stage of an agent's training process to support comparisons between different methods. Validated through experiments in the AI2-Thor framework, this function accurately reflects relative differences in the sample efficiency of various learning strategies. Consequently, analytical predictions align with experimental outcomes, demonstrating that proposed metrics correctly identify the relative sample efficiency of tested approaches.

We investigate the rate at which the Bondi mass can change and determine the specific conditions limiting this evolution. Within Einstein's framework of gravity, the general case yields $|\dot{M}| \leq 4\pi/ \kappa \cdot \max(\sqrt{\lambda}\,T_c)$, where $\dot{M}$ represents the time derivative of the Bondi mass, $\lambda$ is the cosmic string linear mass density, and $T_c$ is critical temperature. Conversely, in string theory's specific context, the derived bound signifies energy release mechanisms tied to cosmic string dynamics, suggesting potential observational signatures or theoretical implications.

This paper proposes a data-driven approach for modeling and controlling grid-connected energy storage systems (ESS) located in rural areas, eliminating the need for extensive parameter knowledge. First, a reduced-order nonlinear battery model is developed using the extended stochastic variable parameter modeling (eSVRM) technique, specifically tailoring key kinetic variables for efficiency. Simulation results utilizing actual measurement and monitoring data confirm that the RHC scheme achieves superior performance compared to conventional model-predictive and rule-based control methods, while the ESS modeling process requires approximately 1% of the time needed for conventional equivalent circuit modeling.

We examine transport in topological insulators that are limited by dislocations. The analysis reveals a novel phenomenon wherein a current flowing parallel to the surface generates new paths through the material's edge, effectively funneling topological surface states into line defects situated directly beneath the interface. This mechanism arises from a linear ramping of the band gap near the dislocation line, transitioning from a finite bulk gap to a zero gap specifically at the location where the defect emerges. The article provides a comprehensive investigation of transport properties resulting in an energy-dependent conductance that exhibits both radial symmetry and angular variation. Additionally, the study identifies a singular point defect in the conductance map that correlates with the specific type (edge or mixed) of the dislocation, with theoretical predictions verified against simulations based on the Landau-Luttington Hamiltonian modified to include elastic strain.

This study investigates the joint extreme behavior of wind speed and significant wave height within the North East Atlantic using a univariate peaks-over-threshold approach. Findings indicate that extremal spatial dependence exhibits slight attenuation with distance, ranging from an asymptotic limit of approximately 0.8 with no adjustment to around values between -0.1 and -0.2 when an inverse exponential model is applied. Additionally, return periods for simultaneous high values of wind speed and wave height are marginally longer than those observed for wave height alone.

Driven by the intermediate Lang conjectures regarding hyperbolicity and rational points, we establish new finiteness theorems for non-constant maps from and to fixed varieties defined over a number field, assuming the varieties satisfy specific geometric conditions. Our approach utilizes boundedness results for maps between varieties with bounded invariants, a method developed by Campana and now central to this approach.

Manipulation ellipsoids provide valuable insights into a human's capabilities and can be utilized for robot instruction, including the emulation of natural movements. While prior methods for this process typically rely on inverse kinematics, our proposed method leverages the manipulability ellipsoid instead. This new approach is applied to a haptic telemanipulation system, where it generates smooth trajectories that mirror human motion by mapping the user's hand movements directly to robotic ones based on ellipsoid properties. The system was utilized to emulate surgical trajectories during a laparoscopic gallbladder dissection, with resulting experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this robot teaching methodology.

This study investigates non-calcule, high-energy particle collider Higgs boson pair production in the di-photon decay channel. Our analysis, which employs QCD NLO calculations and incorporates EFT and BSM extensions up to two loops, reveals that these factors significantly influence the Higgs pair production cross-section. Consequently, our findings offer valuable insights for interpreting current and future LHC experimental data.

We present an approach for learning single-view 3D object pose estimation that leverages large collections of in-the-wild video footage. Our strategy involves generating synthetic training pairs by manipulating these videos: we generate novel top-down views and apply 2D-to-3d pose markers. These synthetic labels are then refined through self-correction against the original source material to eliminate artifacts introduced during synthesis. Additionally, when video content features objects with unambiguous poses, our method utilizes them for further refinement. Leveraging publicly available datasets such as Human-VGA, UVA-3LP, and T2P-3D—which total over 1.2 million images—yields a robust general-purpose 3D pose estimator. Our models achieve state-of-the-art single-view results on the MPII 3D-Human benchmark and establish novel 3D automotive pose records on the UVA-3LP dataset. The methodology is versatile and can be effectively applied to diverse object classes.

This research investigates the mechanisms behind the acceptance of, or rejection toward, COVID-19 vaccine misinformation. It features an original dataset containing rejection and acceptance ratings for 35 distinct pieces of misinformation, drawn from social media and news sources between March and June 2021. The study demonstrates that a neural network model utilizing the BERT architecture and pre-trained on Wikipedia outperforms both traditional machine learning models and smaller baseline models in predicting these ratings. Furthermore, the analysis identifies that the most influential textual characteristics driving misinformation rejection are related to emotional expressions and claims concerning human rights.

Attosecond science has seen rapid advancement in recent years, driven by the capabilities of high-order harmonic sources which deliver pulse durations in the sub-100 femtosecond regime and flux levels reaching the photon level. To further propel this field, there is a critical necessity for improving harvest from harmonic emission by achieving higher conversion efficiencies and higher photon flux, as well as extending harmonic emission to higher frequencies. Recently, resonant atomic excitation has emerged as a promising strategy to achieve these objectives. This review examines the fundamental mechanisms of this phenomenon and explores its significant applications in harmonic attosecond science.

Ephemerides for eclipsing binaries are typically built from the premise that eclipse timing follows a linear progression, punctuated by anomalies attributed to gravitational interactions within their systems or refractive medium issues. Yet, some binaries exhibit cyclical deviations in their observed eclipse times that cannot be explained by standard interactions. This study reports the discovery of cyclic variations in eclipse intervals for W UMa-type contact eclipsing binary AE Aur, detected through over a century of observational data spanning 104 years. Both photometric analyses of recent observations and comprehensive visual parabolic fits were employed to investigate these deviations. Results indicate a cycle period of 17.3 years, aligning the most recent observational data with predictions from the eclipsing orbit model. The authors suggest that azimithal orbital motion of the components, potentially stemming from hydrodynamic effects and angular momentum exchanges between the stars, offers a mechanism for this behavior. Furthermore, the study posits that similar orbit distortions could exist in other eclipsing systems, a factor currently overlooked in the exoplanet detection methodologies used for such objects.

This paper establishes mass-supercritical scattering for the energy-critical Schrödinger equation under negative energy and mass-focusing conditions, specifically for the non-energy-critical portion. This finding extends previous work by Takaishi and the author, which addressed similar scenarios but excluded the mass-supercritical focusing case. The proof relies on two primary strategies: first, deriving precise $\ell^2$-decaying answers for linear equations with potentials and applying them to energy-critical solutions via an approximation approach; second, employing an efficient mechanism to manage potential energy contributions. A significant outcome of this study is the construction of an explicit, decaying potential profile that mirrors the behavior of solutions in the mass-critical regime, a result derived from an $\ell^2$-based approach. These findings collectively enhance our understanding of how solutions in critical and mass-focusing contexts interact with potential-dependent energies.

Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) represent a promising alternative to conventional numerical methods for solving physics-governed partial differential equations (PEDs). Although showing great potential, these approaches depend heavily on defining an effective loss function. Existing strategies for constructing PINNs fall into two categories: manual design and adaptive generation via a tree of subnetworks. The latter offers flexibility but incurs added computational costs. The authors introduce a fully automatic framework utilizing the Weighted Residual Method and a novel algorithm for physically-consistent mesh adaptation. This method dynamically refines both mesh placement and element weights during optimization to enhance solution accuracy. While inspired by Level Set methods, the proposed approach differs by performing adaptations directly within the latent space. The framework's efficacy is validated through applications to linear heat equations and the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations.

Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) are emerging as promising successors to conventional MOSFETs, leveraging the unique negative capacitance effect in ferroelectric heterostructures to achieve ultra-low power dissipation. Despite this advantage, engineering a stable and robust negative capacitance effect remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing a two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric material, $BaZrO_3$ (BZO), integrated with graphene. Our findings indicate that the BZO/graphene heterostructure exhibits strong electrostatic coupling and a pronounced negative capacitance effect, with a maximum voltage amplification factor of 1.82. Furthermore, incorporating this layer into graphene-based field-effect transistor (FeFET) configurations boosts the drain voltage swing from 0.6 V to 1.1 V. These results suggest that BZO/graphene heterostructures hold significant promise for the development of next-generation low-power logic devices.

This study examines real-world attacks within Cargo, detailing their mechanisms and impact, while proposing defensive strategies to mitigate them.

Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) have largely replaced traditional orientation-based methods like SIFT and HOG in image recognition. However, recent orientation-based approaches are gaining traction as they offer superior model interpretability and the ability to optimize specific task-oriented features efficiently. This paper advances the field by introducing Orientation Convolutional Networks (OCNs)—a mechanism generating orientation-specific feature maps through oriented filtering—and a matching Orientation Convolutional Neural Network Training (OCNTN) framework. Both components have been integrated into the open-source TACO library. This work evaluates OCNs across various orientations (9, 16, and 32) using three major benchmarks: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Stanford Dogs. Results demonstrate that an OCN with 16 orientations achieves accuracy rivaling a standard DCNN equivalent on CIFAR-10, surpasses FastFCN on the Stanford Dogs dataset, and outperforms both DCNNs and recent orientation-based legacy methods on CIFAR-100.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are increasingly applied to learning on point clouds, yet the efficacy of these models is often hindered by the high memory usage and low computational efficiency of existing graph construction methods. This paper presents a new framework designed to optimize the building process of graph-based GNNs. The proposed method improves memory efficiency by applying a self-loop to transform edge attributes within the adjacency matrix into self-isolated features, thereby eliminating redundant edge data. Furthermore, it enhances inference speed by replacing complex graph convolutions with standard convolutional layers. Experiments conducted on various point cloud datasets demonstrate that this approach surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques in both accuracy and computational performance.

The traditional host-based Trojan attack typically relies on triggers like system commands or network activity, which can be easily evaded through attack-specific trigger detection. This paper introduces a novel host-independent attack model in which triggers exist solely within the attacker's infrastructure. The target system has no knowledge of, nor does it interact with, these triggers, allowing the payload to execute without user intervention. The authors outline the attack's principles, evaluation metrics, and proposed defenses. The paper concludes with the development of an experimental system that successfully demonstrates this attack, providing the first concrete instance of its realization.

The IFU attached to the Subaru Telescope's Hyper Supernova (Hyper-Supernova) survey instrument, the Redshift Optical Survey for the IFU (ROSIE), was commissioned in 2019. This 2D integral field spectrograph captures light across the H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$ emission lines, covering a field of view measuring 1.8" $\times$ 2.4". During a 10-minute exposure, the device achieves a spectral resolution of approximately 2.5 in the near-infrared (NIR) and yields a spatial granularity of 0.5".

The primary objective of the commissioning phase was to validate the instrument's performance and establish initial reduction protocols. Utilizing M31 as a stellar nucleus standard for testing, the team developed a new pipeline to handle raw data reduction. This process includes steps for removing instrumental profiles, correcting geometric distortions, and performing deconvolution. Validation of the results was achieved by comparing these findings with M31's properties derived from literature, ground-based observations, and space-based observations from Hubble.

This study reports the first successful simulation of carbon-carbon fusion using quantum Monte Carlo methods. The calculation utilized the $J$-adapted, full configuration interaction quantum Montency (FM-QMC) approach within a $j$-shell model, covering all $j$-couplings involving nucleons 1 through 6. By applying a variational method to the energy of the resulting eight-nucleon system cloud, the binding energy of the most probable $\alpha$-cluster configuration was minimized. The resulting predicted binding energy for the $^{13}$C nucleus aligns closely with experimental values, and the most probable cluster count derived from these simulations corresponds exactly to the integer nearest the value of $Z/4$.

Understanding the mass and radius composition of exoplanets is essential for characterizing planetary systems, particularly for terrestrial worlds where bulk composition dictates formation and evolutionary pathways. A critical factor in determining composition is the volatile content, which is often inferred from the devolatilisation of rocky cores during thermal or dynamical evolution—a process that leaves a distinctive signature in the planet's final state. This study presents a model of devolatilisation for rocky exoplanets, offering a method to estimate interior silicate metal fractions from observable radius and mass data. Our approach is grounded in a thermal evolution framework that calculates core temperatures over time, incorporating initial volatile abundances, planet mass, and thermal conductivity. By applying this model, researchers can estimate a planet's primordial water content based on its current mass-radius relationship. Crucially, the model accounts for water accumulation in a overlying mantle layer that remains hydrated but unmixed with the deeper core, a configuration that yields a unique mass-radius signature. When combined with recent observational data on Kepler-10b and Kepler-131b, this technique offers a pathway to constrain the volatile reservoirs of rocky exoplanets, a capability that will be further enhanced by upcoming missions such as TESS, JWST, and Earth's twin exomoon hunter, LUVOIR.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) utilizing raw channel state information (CSI) have recently demonstrated high accuracy in wireless localization. Nevertheless, integrating raw data directly often results in significant deep learning models that are difficult to deploy practically. Our observations indicate that manually engineered features derived from raw CSI can effectively replace the raw data themselves for localization tasks. We introduce CSI mapping, a lightweight feature extraction method designed to reduce both the number of input features and total model parameters. To validate the approach, we implemented the technique using wideband CSI across various deep learning architectures. Experimental results show that CSI mapping achieves accurate localization performance with drastically smaller model footprints compared to direct raw CSI inputs, outperforming manually created heuristic features. Furthermore, we examined how different signal processing methods and channel estimation errors influence the stability and accuracy of the proposed framework.

We examine the connection between the syntactic framework of modal logic and the semantics defined within topological Category $CTop$. Our analysis reveals that the rules corresponding to conjunction, disjunction, and negation align with operations in discrete $T_0$ topological structures, while the interaction involving the modal operators $\Box$ and $\Diamond$ involves more complex topological relationships.

A strong edge-edge coloring of a graph $G$ entails assigning colors to its edges such that every pair of adjacent vertices shares a color set of at least $|V(G)|$ distinct colors. The minimum number of colors needed for such a scheme is denoted as $\text{ecs}(G)$. This parameter can be viewed as a form of edge-edge coloring that mirrors the logic of standard vertex coloring. In this study, we examine general properties of $\text{ecs}(G)$ and provide specific bounds for various graph families, including complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs, circulant graphs, and mesh networks. Additionally, we investigate how $\text{ecs}(G)$ behaves under graph compositions such as the Cartesian product, strong product, and join.

We demonstrate that the eigenvalues of the corresponding $n \times q$ block matrix are $n(q-1)$ and the first $(1-q)^{q-1}$ eigenvalues, each repeated with a multiplicity of the binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{1}$. I am introducing ShinyCOPASI, an web-based tool that integrates COPASI, which is recognized as a comprehensive suite for modeling and analyzing biochemical networks. By combining COPASI's robust technical capabilities with Shiny's powerful capabilities for creating interactive HTML applications, this application allows users to control COPASI functions directly from a web browser. The development of ShinyCOPASI was driven by the need to make COPASI's advanced features more accessible to researchers without the requirement of a local installation. The following sections provide an introduction to the application, outline its key features and use cases, and discuss the challenges encountered during its development.

Neural networks have become the standard for addressing problems in computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. Unlike other inference methods, however, they struggle to provide meaningful explanations for their outputs. This paper introduces a framework quantifying uncertainty to assess the confidence of neural network predictions. The proposed approach integrates a variational autoencoder with a convolutional neural network, where the latter maps image patches to the latent space of the former. The resulting distribution characterizes every input, enabling a decision-making process. This method is distinctively capable of handling uncertainty arising from approximating intractable posterior distributions within neural networks, as opposed to only addressing input-based uncertainty. Evaluation on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrates that the solution outperforms current approaches for unbounded regression tasks and matches the precision of leading approaches used in object detection. The source code will be released publicly.

We investigate the $K_1$-theory of a standard inclusion of compact quantum groups that are K-mathematically diagonal, demonstrating how the $K_1$-theory of their free product relates directly to the $K_1$-theory of the constituent parts. These techniques generalize naturally to demonstrate that for any finite sequence of inclusions of such groups, the resulting map on $K_1$-theory is quasi-split; this establishes both an exact relationship on K-theory groups and provides a specific Künnith formula for the tensor product of their algebras regarding $K$-theory groups. These findings are applied specifically to the theory of free inclusions arising from finite free group actions on their respective algebras.

We introduce an on-policy learning algorithm designed for Markov decision processes (MDPs) that scale to millions of states and transitions. The method exploits the inherent sparsity in the state space, enabling both sample and parameter efficiency. Specifically, it minimizes the need for extensive exploration while requiring only a linear number of variables relative to the count of reachable states. At its core, the approach employs an adaptive importance sampling strategy to estimate state visitation frequencies and utilizes regression techniques to approximate value functions. This strategy underpins a new MDP solver that integrates Monte Carlo methods with online dynamic programming, effectively combining the robust state-space handling of Monte Carlo with the rapid convergence of dynamic programming.

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a weighted oriented graph with edge ideal $I(\mathcal{D})$. We demonstrate that for a specified class of oriented trees $\mathcal{D}$, the ordinary and symbolic powers of this ideal are always equivalent. Furthermore, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions ensuring the equality between these powers specifically for lines equipped with their natural orientations.

Computer models are frequently utilized to generate the synthetic datasets required for statistical analysis. This study introduces a non-parametric method to assess the bias and bias deviation of estimators producing $\theta$-quantiles of rainfall-runoff relationships, where the associated distributions are unknown and the bias of a estimator for $\theta$-quantiles of the true distribution is denoted as $\beta_\theta$. The simulation framework, designed to create synthetic hydrological flow data, was developed by Garcia, Hidalgo, and Sanchez (2007). Our proposed estimator outperforms existing alternatives in terms of bias, showcasing superior overall efficiency. The method's validity is supported through extensive simulation studies.

We investigate the robust learning framework introduced by Goldwasser et al. (STOC 2021), wherein a learner interacts with an adversary to identify a target concept from various distributions. In each turn, the adversary positions themselves within the conceptual space and arranges the distribution to be distribution-robust centered on that location; subsequently, the concept is drawn from this distribution. Upon making predictions, the adversary may corrupt only labels for misclassified examples. The adversary's strategy is constrained by the requirement of sample efficiency, ensuring the distribution and prediction modification remain limited per prediction opportunity. The model's training concludes once the adversary can no longer induce learning failures exceeding a specific robust loss threshold.

The adversary's constraints are measured by the quantity of prediction instances required to cause such failures, termed the robustness budget. We demonstrate that a model equipped with the ability to perform private nearest-point queries within the adversary's distributional support can achieve robust training in linear time regarding the robustness budget. The query privacy constraint mandates the adversary maintain the model's unawareness of the query locations until they are revealed following the distributional adjustment. Conversely, we establish that without such privacy constraints for the adversary, inducing distribution-robust training takes superlinear time relative to the robustness budget in certain scenarios. Our approach also subsumes the results of recent adversary frameworks utilizing stochastic or deterministic perturbations.

This study reports, for the first time, measurements of jet fragmentation functions in both pp and central PbPb interactions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76$ TeV. Lead-lead collisions exhibit significant suppression of jet yields alongside modified jet fragmentation functions compared to proton-proton collisions. These observations are analyzed using the MC@NLO Monte Carlo simulation, which incorporates in-medium parton showering and hard scattering processes. The findings offer insights into the mechanisms of jet production and the dense medium effects within the context of the LHC energy scale.

Inverse Ap\'ery-type (or Ap\'ery-type inverse) binomial series strings have gained significant attention due to their utility in computing the constant terms of several fundamental binomial series. This study calculates the constant terms for multiple binomial series involving multiple inverse Ap\'ery-type (or Ap\'ery-type inverse) binomial series strings featuring variables, as well as establishes numerous closed-form expressions for various multilevel super-levels (or harmonic levels) of binary matrix equations. Additionally, the paper examines the convergence conditions for these series strings.

Its extreme temperature is confirmed by distinct spectral traits, specifically a W1-W2 color of 0.90 and a Spitzer M-J2.2 = 1.01, marking the first identification of a brown dwarf with a Spitzer M-J2.2 index exceeding 0.88. We describe the formation of the hottest and densest matter created to date in high-energy proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider. Our analysis of this system, which has a very short lifetime of approximately 1 femtosecond and small spatial dimensions, reveals that even at the earliest stages, system-size effects are negligible. We demonstrate that the resulting evolution aligns with hydrodynamics, exhibiting similar characteristics to the expansion of larger proton-nucleus and nucleus-nucleus systems. Specifically, the observed radial flow depends on multiplicity rather than geometric size, and the momentum anisotropy generated in the initial stage of expansion matches hydrodynamical expectations. Furthermore, we explore how this system may serve to investigate potential differences in fundamental interactions between quarks and anti-quarks.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for calculating parton distribution functions (PDFs), deriving them as the eigenfunctions of the Boer-Mulders function in longitudinal momentum space. The study establishes a comprehensive framework for analyzing polarized distributions and twist-2 semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) processes. Specifically, the proposed side-by-side presentation first presents this theoretical approach and theory, followed by PDF predictions generated using this new method. Furthermore, the paper includes predictions for unpolarized and polarized PDFs, as well as the Boer-Mulders function $H_1^{T}$$^{\perp}$, derived from global fits incorporating unpolarized structure functions, twist-2 structure functions, and the Boer-Mulders function itself.

Cylindrical samples composed of Martian and Lunar regolith were subjected to sintering at temperatures ranging from 600°C to 1100°C in increments of 100°C using Solaris 1K solar simulators. Following compression testing to assess mechanical properties, the failure zones were examined via optical and scanning electron microscopy. The investigation revealed that Martian and Lunar regolith require an optimal sintering temperature of approximately 800°C to achieve the necessary compressive strength for habitation modules on Mars and the Moon. The failure mechanisms observed in the samples included microcrack propagation and regolith particle pullout.

This study examines the liquid-solid interaction interface within a moving cylindrical film on a fiber, investigating how surface tension and slip phenomena influence flow dynamics. By solving the governing equations for an inviscid, incompressible fluid, perturbation solutions were derived to assess their evolution over time and space. The analysis reveals an initial exponential growth in these disturbances before the onset of viscos effects, with growth intensities modulated by both pressure and slip parameters. Specifically, liquid-solid slip accelerates the growth speed of these perturbations, causing the film to experience breakup more rapidly and break into droplets at a shorter duration. The numerical outcomes presented align well with theoretical predictions regarding the impact of slip conditions.

We conducted an analysis of star formation rates (SFR) in the nearby spiral NGC 4217 by comparing observations of the Br$\beta$ hydrogen recombination line with 1.4 GHz radio continuum data. Our study involved creating a 1D model of the star-forming disk, utilizing Br$\beta$ to determine the intrinsic luminosity and SFR while using the radio continuum to map the galactic disk's geometry. We found that the Br$\beta$ emission originates from a region approximately 1.5~kpc around the center, whereas the radio continuum arises from an extended structure spanning roughly 3.5~kpc. Additionally, the relationship between Br$\beta$ and radio continuum luminosity follows a power law with a slope of $\alpha = 0.85 \pm 0.05$, which is notably shallower than the theoretical expectation of $\alpha = 1.0$. This deviation suggests that using Br$\beta$ as a calibration anchor for SFR from radio observations offers significant potential; however, future research must refine this slope and refine the underlying physical models to fully leverage this method.

The Fisher-KPP equation, first-order extended to include partial derivatives and nonlinearity, describes additive genetic drift or neutral diffusion in population dynamics. Its solutions represent traveling waves of spatial heterogeneity, where wave velocity is determined by the balance between drift/diffusion and nonlinearity. This work provides a rigorous demonstration that the wave velocity derived from the full system aligns precisely with the velocity obtained from its linear approximation. The proof utilizes modern methods of asymptotic analysis, specifically mapping the solution to a constant-coefficient linear system and applying asymptotic assumptions to solve it. These steps allow the rigorous identification of the wave velocity's functional form as $1 + \sqrt{1 + 22}$, matching existing literature.

Based on the 20th-century academic standards, we have developed a binary classifier capable of identifying whether a handwritten symbol represents a mathematical one. The study analyzes the terms' forms using shape-based features and evaluates the system's performance across multiple scenarios. The resulting classifier achieves high accuracy, reaching up to 96.6% performance in semi-supervised tasks involving unfamiliar terms.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for duration modeling in neural Text-to-Speech systems, designed to mitigate the influence of outliers by utilizing a HMM-RNN hybrid architecture that emits a continuous distribution over time. We refine the standard EM-HH-RNN framework by employing permutation-invariant loss functions to train the recurrent component regarily to match the discrete labels from the hidden Markov model. Furthermore, for the refinement of the synthesis, we propose using the median rather than the traditional mean as a duration predictor for post-training. This shift effectively lowers synthesized voice pitch variability and produces more natural-sounding speech. Although the model's inference technically remains in the realm of integers, our use of a regarily-trainrd component during the training phase allows for sampling with linear complexity, facilitating the efficient calculation of the exact median for generation.

Occupancy modeling is a widely employed framework in ecology, utilized to estimate the hidden distribution and abundance of species. Although recognized as a two-stage probabilistic process, practical application frequently simplifies this by decoupling the stages via linearization or Laplace approximation, resulting in a singularly linearized system. This study utilizes simulation data to examine the impact of pre-solving the coexistence equation—commonly referred to as 'pre-solving'—within the full two-stage system. Evidence indicates that applying pre-solving can introduce systematic biases into occupancy and detection rate estimates. While the standard practice of pre-solving remains justified for its efficiency in cases of low species detection probability, the authors propose an alternative approach: iterative solver methods (either Gaussian or Newton-based) tailored for scenarios featuring high detection probabilities. The analysis reveals that when detection probabilities are high, utilizing an iterative solver yields parameter assessments that are less skewed compared to the results from pre-solving.

While Deep Learning (DL) has shown significant success in assisting with the classification of malignant skin lesions in dermatology, current DL-driven diagnostic support systems remain static, lacking dynamic interaction with users. We introduce a novel approach leveraging interactive DL to create a user-centric decision-assist tool. This method incorporates an attention mechanism that allows the system to focus on user-highlighted regions of a skin image. By combining this attention mechanism with two distinct Deep Neural Networks (DNLS)—one for classification and another for identifying explanation regions—the system generates targeted diagnoses. Specifically, the proposed framework refines the standard explanation method by replacing global attention with per-class localization, effectively reducing false positives. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods regarding both classification accuracy and the precision of explanation regions. The source code will be made publicly available.

We introduce a probabilistic autoencoder designed for Type Ia supernovae spectral time series, parameterized by physically meaningful variables. This framework includes a probabilistic flow prior to facilitate physical parameter recovery. The model's components were developed based on prior knowledge: the architecture reflects the causal order of spectral formation, the variance-covariance matrix aligns with observed covariance structures, and the noise distribution matches empirical data characteristics. The flow prior specifically allows the latent space to recombine elemental abundances into various spectral profiles. Applied to simulated data, the system successfully reconstructed both absorption features and emission features while retrieving accurate flow parameters. These capabilities suggest that similar encoders can effectively disentangle physical parameters from real observational spectra, even amidst noise.

We report the detection of a significant neutral gas outflow in the dusty star-forming galaxy HATLASJ085338.9+015537, located at a redshift of $z=2.13$. This discovery stems from deep, high-resolution (0\farcs3) 12mCO observations conducted with the IRAM 30m telescope. The observations reveal a highly extended CO(2–1) outflow spanning at least 1.5 kpc, with a derived atomic gas mass of $\gtrsim 1.5\times10^9$ M$_{\odot}$ and a mass outflow rate exceeding $1.5 M_{\odot}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$. Spatially, the outflowing gas is confined to a plane perpendicular to the galactic disk, a geometry likely dictated by the galaxy's strong vertical gravitational field. While the outflow exhibits a non-uniform CO intensity profile, a simple model fitting this distribution suggests a mean velocity of $\sim 150$ km s$^{-1}$. Given an outflow scalelength of roughly 11 pc, this implies a CO velocity gradient of approximately 11 km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{-1}$, consistent with rotation in a rotating disk. This study investigates the entrainment process in an axisymmetric turbulent plume characterized by unequal mean momentum and buoyancy fluxes, where the momentum and positive or negative (upward or downward) buoyancy discharges are fixed while particle sedimentation provides the buoyancy anomaly. The analysis relies on an extensive dataset of direct numerical simulations covering the full spectrum from laminar to highly turbulent flows. For the particle-laden plumes examined, the effective particle-laden plume buoyancy flux is found to be deterministic, allowing the application of established laminar and turbulent entrainment frameworks. The research demonstrates that the effective plume buoyancy flux is governed by sediment drag, inter-particle collisions, the relative importance of particle-laden jets, and the stabilizing influence of mean shear. The resulting particle-modified entrainment rates are presented as a function of the Stokes number, particle-laden to momentum plume flux ratio, and sediment density relative to the carrier fluid, for both positive and negative buoyancy scenarios.

Diseases spread through intricate networks of interpersonal interactions that are typically represented as standard graphs, where contacts form edges between nodes representing individuals. In contrast, hypergraphs offer a more natural fit for modeling interactions that involve multiple participants simultaneously. This study presents an approach to calculating the spread of disease within hypergraph contact networks, focusing on susceptible-infected-removed (SIR) dynamics. We derive analytic expressions for the early-stage evolution of susceptibility and infection, establishing connections to established graph theory concepts such as generating functions and branching processes. Our findings reveal distinct characteristics of the phase transition within the infection susceptibility, characterized by higher orders and a lack of universality. Furthermore, we executed susceptible-infected (SI) Monte Carlo simulations to validate our analytic predictions, demonstrating excellent agreement across various network topologies—including random unweighted and weighted configurations, as well as preferential attachment models—while applying the model to empirical data from a pig farm regarding influenza A (H1N1v). Finally, we analyzed an artificial scenario involving a university campus to explore the potential advantages of employing SIR dynamics within a student hypernetwork.

The spin canting effect has been demonstrated in a two-dimensional magnetic semiconductor, specifically CrI$_3$. Employing a first-principles approach, researchers found that this anisotropy arises from the exchange interaction between out-of-plane magnetic moments, a process facilitated by in-plane d-d orbital overlap. This exchange coupling is expected to induce spincanting in other bilayer van der Waals magnetic semiconductors as well. The presence of such canting offers new avenues to manipulate magnetic properties through the application of electric fields and provides a potential pathway to reexamining and understanding the three-dimensional bulk exchange interactions in chromium iodide.

This study investigates rotation differentials in solar-type stars, specifically those with surface Rossby numbers (Ro) of 0.01 to 0.1, utilizing a spherically coordinate-invariant $\alpha\Omega$ dynamo model. This model is built upon the Boussinesq approximation and incorporates the $\beta$-effect, which accounts for rotational instability. We demonstrate that the magnitude of the $\beta$-effect is critical in this regime, as it stabilizes the differential rotation profile, rendering it less sheared as the Rossby number decreases (i.e., making rotation more uniform). This relationship establishes a clear connection between a star's rotation regularity and its $\beta$-effect strength. Furthermore, this proposed mechanism offers a coherent framework to explain the observed contrast in differential rotation between the Sun and other G-type stars, such as $\alpha$ Cen A and $\tau$ Con A.

Multimodal input is becoming increasingly vital for human-machine interaction, though existing models often require heavy reliance on manual feature engineering. This work introduces a K-fan deep architecture designed to automatically learn representations from unimodal data and integrate them effectively. By utilizing a specific merging mechanism, the model aligns and combines these single-modulus representations. A distinct attribute of our proposed framework is its **unified approach** to various tasks, eliminating the need to pre-train on specific tasks. We assessed the model across four diverse applications: one-layer and two-autoencoder variants, successfully demonstrating state-of-the-art or competitive performance in autoencoding tasks, as well as achieving strong results in multi-label classification and face recognition. Additionally, we established a new benchmark for face representation learning using two autoencoder architectures. Finally, experiments with a K-fan classification model achieved high accuracy on two challenging datasets: 2D face age estimation and estimating 3D human pose from images.

Model checking serves as an effective technique for uncovering subtle concurrency faults in programs that unit and functional tests often miss in multi-threaded environments. This paper introduces the introduction of Spiny Ark, a Spiny Framework library designed to integrate model checking directly into standard development workflows. Spiny Ark leverages the Scala program verifier, verified by the SMT solver, to automatically generate and execute detailed execution paths. The underlying approach is demonstrated here as a practical instance of applying formal verification to real-world software, with Spiny Ark's source code available for public review.

WhatsApp has emerged as the primary platform for global messaging, yet it lacks effective mechanisms to curb misinformation once it has taken hold. Our lack of control over content within these closed networks presents a significant challenge, as it is difficult to identify false narratives before they escalate. Consequently, our objective is to detect the initial points where deception spreads. To achieve this, we employ an approach that combines data collection with the analysis of message threads. By applying Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, we can characterize threads based on their content, even when the direct text is obscured by links. This allows for the retrieval of full context via web scraping once a link is identified within a thread. We implemented this strategy on Brazilian networks, selecting threads that exhibited high interaction levels to filter out those unconnected to misinformation episodes. By comparing the linguistic features of threads tagged as misinformation against benign threads, we identified the specific elements triggering false spread. Our analysis reveals that the closed ecosystem of WhatsApp facilitates a rapid escalation of deception, a phenomenon amplified by the algorithmic prioritization of reactive messages such as emojis and sharing activities.

This study investigates a model of a general branching population in which individuals of a continuous type, represented by $X(t)$, evolve over time. The frequencies of these individuals within the total population constitute a stochastic process that acts as a martingale, converging almost surely as $t \to \infty$ to a limiting value; this limit is either the uniform distribution across types or results in the extinction of the population type. The convergence is characterized by either the survival of the population or the emergence of a dominant type. The framework encompasses general scenarios, including those with frequency-dependent fitness, and applies to various functional forms such as countable types, locally compact Abelian groups, general topological spaces, and metric spaces. The primary goal of spoofing detection systems is to identify synthetic artifacts generated through synthesis or playback attacks. This paper evaluates the attention rectified linear unit (AReLU), which integrates a synthetic data strategy into its data representation model. This architecture combines spatial and temporal signal features into a single, streamlined format. The study assesses the AReLU-based model on the ASVspoof 2019 Bank task using the proposed feature set. Experimental results indicate that the AReLU unit enhances the model's robustness against the provided test matrices.

Supergravity presents unique constraints on building inflation models that distinct from global supersymmetry. This difficulty arises because the mechanism responsible for accelerating expansion in inflation often conflicts with ensuring a consistent, anomaly-free local supersymmetric structure. In this work, I introduce a novel model where inflation and anomaly cancellation are seamlessly realized by exploiting features of the $E_7 \times E_7$ U-duality within the heterotic $O(16) \times E_8$ string framework. Specifically, a U-duality rotation is applied to construct an intermediate vacuum possessing unbroken $E_7 \times E_7$ symmetry. Within this manifold, the model demonstrates that the conditions for anomaly cancellation and inflation can be simultaneously met.

Nonreciprocal optical systems are essential for photonic devices like optical isolators and circulators, yet their fundamental connection to quantum correlations has not been fully explored. This study investigates nonreciprocal features in first- and second-order joint correlations of twin optical beams passing through nonreciprocal optical arrangements. Our findings reveal a parallel between the theoretical limits of quantum nonlocality and physical nonreciprocities, specifically within energy-time twin-beam correlations. Our relationship holds generally and includes a specific case for the Mollow triplet's first-order spectrum, demonstrating that while first-order spectra remain symmetric in the forward and backward directions, second-order joint correlations can differ between these directions. Furthermore, these joint correlations can exhibit strong nonlocality regarding the time slots of both photons and can even violate the principle of detailed balance.

Superconducting quantum circuits have emerged as a leading platform in quantum computing, yet they remain constrained by the intrinsic flaws of the physical materials used to construct quantum bits (qubits). The research community has recently intensified its focus on circuit layout strategies to improve interface quality and lower error rates. This study presents a specific case analysis of a two-qubit system, utilizing circuit Larmor dephasing (LDD) measurements to investigate how circuit components contribute to overall qubit coherence. The location of the LDD drive signal was systematically varied to probe the circuit's geometric sensitivity, revealing strong site-dependent responses that offer compelling support for an inductive coupling model. Notably, some positions produced markedly lower qubit response, a phenomenon attributed to the suppression of magnetic flux penetration into the loop area. These findings underscore how fundamental insights into circuit architecture can be extracted from circuit-level measurement data, providing crucial guidance for designing more coherent qubits with superior coherence properties.

Regarding the partitioning of $\mathbb{R}$ into Borel sets, Hausdorff demonstrated the existence of uncountable partitions where no two subsets are similar, a finding that stands in contrast to Erdos and Tardos's later result concerning the similar subsets found when $\mathbb{R}$ is replaced with a partition of $\mathbb{N}$ under a different set theoretic hypothesis. This paper presents an alternative subset theoretic assumption, which is independent of the continuum hypothesis, that is also useful for constructing a model in which the analog of the Hausdorff theorem remains valid within $\mathbb{N}$, thereby ensuring there are no two similar subsets under their respective conditions.

Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) are widely recognized for their ability to generate positive risk-adjusted returns, yet the specific trading strategies enabling this success remain elusive. This study examines whether the trade-reconstruction approach, previously associated with CTAs, is actually driven by the behavior of short-term reversal traders. The evidence indicates that CTAs profit significantly by buying assets these traders sell and vice versa. Furthermore, the reconstruction of individual trades reveals that CTAs execute both long and short positions in response to information releases that reversal traders process differently than the average investor. Ultimately, the research suggests that the phenomenon of short-term reversal trading serves as a crucial component in understanding the source of CTAs' trading profitability.

Protocol detection involves the critical network security task of identifying the application layer protocol to enable proper protocol-specific inspection. However, prevalent detection methods struggle with precision due to the diverse challenges inherent in this domain. This paper presents an examination of the difficulties protocol detection entails, along with corresponding mitigation strategies. Additionally, we introduce a neural network-based method for enhancing protocol detection, validated using a newly developed dataset, the QUIC-HTTP3, specifically tailored for the QUIC and next-generation HTTP protocols.

Recent years have seen intense research into magnetic insulators, which host spin-waves known as magnons. Due to their inherent properties, magnons represent a promising carrier for information that could lead to significant advancements in computing and storage technologies. The following text provides a brief overview of the ongoing development of all-optical techniques for controlling magnons—a capability essential for integrating magnonic systems with other functional components—and concludes with a perspective on future prospects in this field.

Federated learning emerges as a promising approach to distributed machine learning, ensuring user privacy by avoiding the transfer of sensitive data while facilitating the acquisition of diverse datasets. While prior investigations have primarily examined its efficacy across independent data sources, this study delves deeper into performance variations within non-identically distributed environments. Specifically, we analyze two common statistical assumptions—concept drift and covariate shift—and evaluate their impact on model outcomes. By proposing novel methodologies to characterize both types of drift, we offer insights into mitigating their adverse effects. Our comprehensive experimental suite covers various concepts of drift alongside state-of-the-art aggregation algorithms to ensure robust comparisons. Drawing from popular benchmark datasets, we establish a thorough evaluation framework to contrast our proposed metrics against existing ones. Ultimately, this work offers valuable perspectives on the impact of data shift on federated learning efficiency and introduces measurable metrics capable of predicting performance losses caused by concept drift.

This Letter introduces a theoretical framework designed for comprehensive optical analysis of high-dimensional Greenberger-Horne-Zeinberger (GHZ) resources. The study initially validates this methodology through complete measurements of distinct three-photon GHZ states within a tripartite quantum basis. The approach is subsequently generalized, with a full photonic hyper-entanglement and quantum Fourier transform integration. The utility of this proposal for enhancing information capacity in quantum communication systems is finally highlighted.

This study proposes an innovative joint active-passive learning algorithm designed to optimize user positioning and Intelligent-Reflecting-Surface (IRS) phase shifts for reducing uplink (UL) channel estimation errors. Built upon a Bayesian learning framework, the work addresses two core challenges: (1) the joint optimization of UL beamforming and IRS configuration to minimize a regularized UL mean squared learning error (MSLE) of channel coefficients, and (2) the development of low-complexity solutions through the integration of a genetic search for discrete user locations with the Alternating Projection Method (APM) for continuous phase shift updates. The resulting comprehensive algorithm effectively enhances spectral efficiency by leveraging a two-stage transmission protocol and successively deriving approximate closed-form expressions (via Taylor series) and simplified forms of the continuous variables within the iterative loop.

Between March and May 2020, the authors analyzed 1.3 million articles from over 1,000 U.S. local news outlets to examine how media coverage of COVID-19 evolved geographically and demographically. The study reveals distinct temporal patterns: while early reporting emphasized travel and general information, coverage shifted toward a focus on testing and treatment as the pandemic progressed. Local news volumes initially tracked national death rates but eventually declined independently. Furthermore, the intensity of local news was strongly influenced by whether the city had a major university, suggesting the role of such institutions in driving early information-seeking.

Counting represents a critical milestone in human cognitive development, a process whose individual trajectory remains poorly understood. This study examines the learning dynamics of a single child to fill that knowledge gap. We analyze a dataset comprising over 1,000 video clips, in which the child attempts to count objects at varying rates. By applying Gaussian Process Regression models, we identify a distinct inflection in the curriculum of object quantities, shifting from a phase governed by discrete numerical concepts to one dominated by continuous number lines. Furthermore, we introduce a novel neural architecture, Neural ODEs with a Time-Varying Forcing Function (NODEV), capable of emulating the quantification strategies used by the child. This model not only mirrors the developmental phase transition but also generates smooth, quantitative generalizations across different number scales.

Bloom filters are extensively employed to efficiently ascertain whether an element is absent from a set. While cuckoo filters can determine element absence with the same reliability, they also have the distinct ability to return an element's presence with a defined, tunable error probability. This capability makes them exceptionally effective for minimizing redundant data in applications such as DNS caching and cache systems. However, standard implementations of cuckoo filters suffer from linearity in memory access during lookups, a characteristic that hinders performance on modern architectures capable of high-level caching and parallelism. Addressing this, we introduce Packed Cuckoo Filters (PCF), a design optimized for these modern hardware features. By reordering filter operations to maximize data locality and leveraging modern out-of-order, superscalar processors along with hardware bitsets, our approach significantly enhances efficiency. We validate the PCF model across three practical applications, achieving speedups of as much as 10.7$\times$ to 21.6 times compared to the prior state-of-the-art.
